entries.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
entries.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. Applied to an unmodified InGaAs PIN photodiode at room temperature, a 10 us waveform decoded by a neural network reconstructs spectra of one to three laser lines across the 80 nm of the telecom C+L band, locating the lines to 0.3-0.4 nm, counting them in about 99% of measurements and identifying their power levels, with line shifts tracked to tens of picometres. Because OED relies on universal semiconductor transport physics, the approach is material-agnostic and applies in principle to any off-the-shelf photodiode, turning detectors already deployed as power monitors into low-cost spectral sensors.

entries.title: Decision Age: Information Freshness under Fusion Rules in Multi-Sensor Command and Control
entries.abstract: Command and control systems decide automatically on evidence that a fusion rule requires from several sensors. The Age of Information measures how current a datum is when it reaches the fusion node, but existing multi-source results treat additional sources as redundancy: the age at the monitor falls as sources are added. This paper addresses the opposite regime. When a rule demands corroboration the decision waits for the slowest required source, so the binding quantity is a maximum, not a minimum, of source ages. We define the decision age of an arbitrary monotone fusion rule, obtain its distribution in closed form for periodic and event-driven sources, and show that the mean decision age grows linearly with the corroboration level, from the floor of the age sawtooth to its peak. We add a dominance criterion that identifies which sensor governs decision freshness, and a measurement methodology for fielded systems. Freshness becomes a verifiable requirement, and adding sensors is shown to make automatic decisions older rather than fresher.

entries.title: Decision Fusion in Wireless Networks: A Tutorial and Survey of Classical and Learning-Based Methods
entries.abstract: Decision fusion combines local decisions from distributed sensors to support reliable detection of phenomena in wireless networks. The effectiveness of decision fusion depends on sensing accuracy, reporting-channel reliability, and available communications and computation resources. This article surveys decision-fusion techniques for wireless sensor networks and emerging communication systems, bringing together their theoretical foundations and practical implementation requirements. We review network architectures and hard, soft, and quantized reporting strategies, and examine statistical, learning-based, game-theoretic, and heuristic fusion approaches. Advanced fusion techniques, including relay-aware combining, link-adaptive regeneration, branch selection, and likelihood approximations, are discussed with emphasis on their assumptions, information requirements, and limitations. The survey examines tradeoffs among detection performance, computational complexity, communications overhead, energy consumption, and latency. The tradeoffs are considered across representative sensing applications and emerging technologies, including massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication, uncrewed aerial vehicle-assisted networks, and the massive Internet of Things. The reviewed literature highlights the importance of jointly considering sensing quality, reporting reliability, and fusion processing when selecting a suitable strategy. Finally, we identify research directions in resource-aware optimization, uncertainty calibration, and robust learning-based fusion under heterogeneous data, missing reports, and changing wireless conditions. Particular attention is given to convergence, generalization, and the costs of training and inference.

entries.title: Sensor-Free Shockable Rhythm Classification During CPR Using the Existing ECG Channel of Public-Access Automated External Defibrillators
entries.abstract: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs) are public-access devices intended for use by lay rescuers, yet they must pause chest compressions to analyze the rhythm because compressions corrupt the electrocardiogram (ECG). Removing this pause requires a method that uses the hardware already present in the device, fits within its processor budget, and meets the rhythm-recognition performance required for defibrillator approval. Existing approaches rely either on an auxiliary sensor, which entails a hardware redesign, or on an additional network that reconstructs the ECG before classification. This work classifies the compression-contaminated ECG directly, using only the existing ECG channel of the AED. A cascade of three compact convolutional networks trained with different class ratios verifies each decision with a second network biased toward the proposed outcome; disagreement yields an indeterminate outcome. Evaluated on an independent manufacturer-provided cohort of 464 subjects over 15 train-validation partitions, the cascade satisfies both adjudicable American Heart Association criteria under all six noise conditions at an eight-second window and a signal-to-artifact ratio of 0 dB, with sinus-rhythm specificity of 99.20-99.43% and other non-shockable specificity of 95.48-96.20%, leaving only 1.07-1.48% of segments indeterminate. The criteria are not met at -3 dB. Single networks matched in parameter count and inference cost do not reproduce this performance. Each decision evaluates two of the three networks and requires 6.68 ms on a single thread of a general-purpose processor, and eight-bit quantization reduces the model to 1.45 MiB without changing any compliance verdict. Thus, rhythm analysis during ongoing CPR can be implemented with the ECG hardware already present in public-access AEDs, without auxiliary sensing hardware, subject to validation on the target device.

entries.title: Chance-Constrained Joint Beam Hopping Scheduling and Bandwidth Allocation for LEO Satellites
entries.abstract: Service level agreement (SLA) reliability is a key requirement in multibeam satellite systems, where operators must satisfy heterogeneous and time-varying traffic demands using limited resources. Beam hopping (BH) enables flexible resource allocation by activating only a subset of beams at each time slot. However, most existing BH optimization methods rely on predicted channel conditions and do not explicitly control the probability of SLA violation under spectral efficiency uncertainty. This work introduces an SLA-aware chance-constrained BH optimization model for joint beam scheduling and bandwidth allocation. The proposed formulation maximizes the expected delivered traffic while ensuring that each cell demand is satisfied with a target reliability level. By modelling the spectral efficiency prediction error as Gaussian, the probabilistic SLA constraints are reformulated as deterministic second-order cone constraints. Evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains the target SLA reliability under increasing traffic load and spectral efficiency uncertainty, while maintaining fairness and efficient resource allocation.

entries.title: Temporal Contrastive Alignment of EEG and Naturalistic Video Only Beats Linear Decoding On In-Sample Stimuli
entries.abstract: Neural tracking, the temporal alignment between a continuous stimulus and the elicited brain response, enables decoding of attention from electroencephalography (EEG), yet its application to naturalistic video remains largely unexplored and mainly relies on linear canonical correlation analysis (CCA). We investigate whether a temporal contrastive model, pairing pretrained VideoMAE features with a lightweight EEG encoder trained on a correlation-based InfoNCE objective, can strengthen EEG-video alignment. Benchmarked against CCA under three generalization regimes, the model outperforms CCA across subjects (leave-one-subject-out), matches it within the stimulus manifold (leave-video-segment-out), and falls behind CCA when extrapolating to entirely novel videos (leave-one-video-out). Because this advantage appears only for seen stimuli, we probe its basis: a sham control shows that a high accuracy does not certify genuine alignment, as a synthesized correspondence fit to the seen stimuli can reproduce it without genuine temporal alignment in the training pairs. This does not preclude practical use: on a downstream attention-decoding task with seen stimuli, the model remains better than CCA since the decoding only requires a strong statistical coupling, regardless of whether that coupling is physiologically meaningful. Using a group-averaged EEG reference, we further show that genuine, generalizable coupling is nonetheless learned, only buried in the noise of single-subject EEG. These results indicate that progress hinges on data scale, diversity, and single-subject denoising.

entries.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
entries.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) represents the most effective technique for the detection of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. This procedure produces a multi-dimensional signal with hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain location. In this work, we propose a joint Hidden Markov Model (HMM), in which each SEEG channel is described by a latent Markov chain, with states shared across the network and channel-specific transition probabilities. Accordingly, we develop a detection algorithm that identifies the channels belonging to the EZ by quantifying, through the Kullback-Leibler divergence, the difference between their transition probabilities in the inter-ictal period and at seizure onset. We evaluate our framework in SEEG recordings from 30 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and compare it with a benchmark that operates in the same observation space but does not consider a latent-state structure. Compared against medically validated EZ definitions, our study shows that modeling channel-specific temporal transitions can improve EZ localization and offer a data-driven framework to investigate the latent dynamics underlying seizures.

entries.title: Reading Across Space, Time and Frequencies: Tensor Decomposition of SEEG Signals to Support Epileptogenic Zone Definition
entries.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) is an invasive technique used in the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy to support the localization of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ). SEEG data are particularly complex to analyze, as they include hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain site, with interactions varying in both time and frequency. In this study, we propose a new framework for SEEG analysis, based on the Canonical Polyadic (CP) decomposition, to extract the latent modes underlying seizure generation. We model SEEG signals as a third-order tensor (channel x time x frequency), and factorize the tensor into rank-1 factors. We then exploit the channel-specific factor as an unsupervised feature set for identifying the EZ. The framework is validated on SEEG-recorded seizures from 35 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. The results show that the joint combination of multiple frequency bands significantly enhances classification performance.

entries.title: Absolute User Fairness for a Downlink Multiuser MIMO-NOMA System
entries.abstract: User fairness has been widely researched in various non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems. In this paper, max-min or min-max fairness is adopted for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output NOMA system, where one multi-antenna base station (BS) transmits to multiple NOMA clusters and each cluster is composed of two single-antenna users sharing a single beam on the same time-frequency resource block. Specifically, under perfect channel state information in the transmitter (CSIT), max-min fairness is adopted to maximize the minimum achievable rate among all users. Under partial CSIT, i.e., the BS only knows the distance and channel direction information of each user, min-max fairness is adopted to minimize the maximum outage probability among all users. Under either CSIT case, to avoid solving the coupled problem, zero-forcing beamforming is designed to obtain a power control problem and then a binary search or formula based algorithm is proposed. Theoretical analyses reveal that under either CSIT case, the problem can be guaranteed to have a unique solution and the proposed algorithm is computationally efficient due to only simple closed-form expressions involved.

entries.title: SEP Analysis of Fluid Antenna GSC Reception under Correlated Nakagami-m Fading and Imperfect Channel Estimation
entries.abstract: Channel estimation (CE) errors and correlation among the fading channels are two of the most fundamental factors degrading the performance of any multi-antenna system. This paper aims to analytically capture their joint effect on fluid antenna systems (FASs) performing generalized selection combining (GSC), i.e., combining the received signals at the best L of the L available ports using maximum ratio combining (MRC). More specifically, the FAS receiver is subject to arbitrarily correlated Nakagami-m fading channels following the fully correlated Jakes' model, and employs a pilot-aided maximum-likelihood rule for CE prior to data detection. A novel tight moment-matching-based Gamma approximation is proposed for the marginal distribution of the estimated channel gains, which is then used to derive the joint statistics of the estimated correlated channels for the case of non-identical integer or half-integer fading severity parameters. Considering that the transmitter employs M-ary phase-shift keying or quadrature amplitude modulation, the joint statistics are further exploited to obtain exact finite-integral symbol error probability (SEP) expressions for a GSC-based FAS receiver, along with closed-form counterparts for the case of identical fading parameters. In addition, asymptotic SEP expressions at high signal-to-noise ratio are derived, analytically establishing that non-ideal CE and fading correlation degrade only the FAS's coding gain, while the diversity order is preserved and governed solely by the number of combined ports and the estimated fading severity. The presented numerical SEP investigations offer concrete design insights into the trade-offs between CE quality, fading correlation, and port selection for the GSC-based FAS receiver.

entries.title: Channel-Aware Codebook Design for Task-Oriented Token Communication Over Wireless Networks
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive codebook design for task-oriented token communication over wireless networks with dynamic channels. This paper proposes the channel-aware codebook (CAC), a joint channel- and reconstruction-driven framework that reorders the labels of a frozen 14-bit VQGAN codebook. In the considered framework, a balanced geometric partition forms prefix groups, a prefix bijection places the groups on the label hypercube, and bijective suffix assignments place the codewords within each group. The problem is formulated to minimize the expected full-image perceptual distortion of the frozen decoder under a binary symmetric channel, averaged over a design set of bit error rates (BERs) and retaining simultaneous token errors. An offline algorithm alternates prefix and suffix exchanges and screens and confirms candidates on paired batches under a fixed decoder-evaluation budget. The assignment preserves the error-free reconstruction and the payload and deploys as static lookup tables without retraining. Under the binary symmetric channel at BER 0.01, it reduces LPIPS by 12.3% and improves COCO AP by 14.1% (1.72 points) relative to the native labels, and it lowers LPIPS by a further 4.5% relative to a related assignment adaptation at the same payload.

entries.title: Detecting Formation-Preserving GNSS Spoofing of UAV Swarms through Transmitter Parallax in Pseudorange and Doppler
entries.abstract: Swarms of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) detect Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing by checking the drones' reported positions against their known formation. Formation-preserving spoofing evades this check: in GNSS-WASP, one transmitter per satellite, a few kilometres away, shifts the whole swarm while keeping its formation. We show that such an attack still leaves a trace below the position level. Because the transmitters are close, each drone sees them under a slightly different angle, and this parallax bends the signal arrival times across a 90 m swarm by 20-40 cm for a transmitter at 5 km, whatever delays the attacker applies. We propose a likelihood ratio test that reads this trace from the pseudoranges and Doppler every drone already measures, with all clocks and attacker delays unknown and no extra antennas. In simulations with real GPS and Galileo orbits and white receiver noise, 16 drones detect GNSS-WASP at 5 km in 13-60% of 10 s windows in straight flight and in every window during a formation turn with a precise Doppler receiver, where the countermeasure proposed with GNSS-WASP detects at most 5%. The same test also catches single-transmitter and ground-array spoofing.
entries.comment: 16 pages, 7 main figures, 7 main tables. Includes supplementary appendices

entries.title: Blind tests of a simple-body model of submarine target strength on open benchmarks
entries.abstract: Finite-element and boundary-element models of a submarine's sonar echo need a mesh and a solver, and their cost grows quickly with frequency. SSR-Sim takes an analytical route. The hull is cut into a few simple bodies, the echo of each is a closed-form result of geometrical acoustics or of the Kirchhoff approximation, the surface enters through a plane-wave reflection coefficient, and the echoes add in energy. This paper describes the method, including the reduction of a hull and its sail to simple bodies, and tests it on three open cases. (1) The reflection coefficient of a 50 mm rubber tile on steel plating, computed with finite elements by Yang et al., is reproduced to 0.02 rms or better at incidence angles from 0° to 75° once the layer is allowed to refract. (2) For the rigid full-scale BeTSSi submarine at 1 kHz, a prediction fixed before the reference was opened agrees with the boundary-element results of Venås and Kvamsdal to within 0.7 dB in every aspect sector from the bow to 150°; in the stern sector it is 5 dB high. (3) For a 1:15 BeTSSi model with 10 mm tiles measured in a lake, a second blind prediction is within -3.1, +1.4 and -0.5 dB of the measured level over aspects 0-120° at 5, 15 and 20 kHz, against -3.1, +3.1 and +3.5 dB for the Kirchhoff-finite-element computation published with the measurement. At 10 kHz, on a resonance of the tile, the prediction is 6.9 dB low, and in the bow sector it is 7 dB or more low at every frequency. The tests cover the specular component and the coating model only. The failures show what such a model lacks: edge diffraction and the returns that set the off-beam floor of a real model.

entries.title: Feedback-Free FDD Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Sparse AP Activation and Dual-Mode Precoding
entries.abstract: This correspondence enables practical frequency-division duplex (FDD) operation in cell-free massive MIMO via two mechanisms. Sparse access-point (AP) activation reduces downlink pilot overhead to enable coherent detection, while angle-reciprocity precoding steers beams using only uplink-estimated angles, eliminating channel feedback entirely. A load-adaptive dual-mode optimizer further enhances performance: closed-form signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio precoding for high-load rate boosting, or semidefinite relaxation for low-load power minimization. Simulations verify its superiority over existing feedback-free FDD solutions in spectral and energy efficiency, and its robustness to angle errors, reciprocity mismatch, and multipath.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology

entries.title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
entries.abstract: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training. To encourage cooperation without inter-device communication, a shared global reward aligned with system cost is employed. Extensive simulations demonstrate rapid convergence and significant improvement in overall system cost compared with baselines, e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN).
entries.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

entries.title: DISC: A Deterministic Instantaneous-SINR Combiner for Uplink Massive MIMO Systems
entries.abstract: Future Massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems will fit more antennas into compact arrays, making minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) combining computationally demanding. Maximum-ratio (MR) combining serves as a cheaper alternative but performs poorly in multi-user scenarios. Existing solutions to this either mimic the MMSE combiner using second-order statistics or, as in the optimal bilinear equalizer (OBE), rely on the loose use-and-then-forget (UaTF) bound. In this paper, we propose DISC, a novel receive combiner that instead maximizes a deterministic approximation of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), obtained by replacing the random terms in the SINR with deterministic equivalents. This approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the number of antennas grows, and it exploits useful information discarded by the UaTF bound. The computational complexity of DISC matches that of OBE, with the low-complexity variant DISC-D being even cheaper than conventional MR combining. We further prove that the SINR achieved by DISC grows unbounded with the number of antennas, even under pilot contamination, similarly to MMSE combining. Finally, we numerically demonstrate that DISC achieves a sum spectral efficiency close to that of MMSE combining under full pilot sharing, while outperforming other combiners across signal-to-noise ratio, pilot length, and spatial correlation models.

entries.title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
entries.abstract: Cross-environment deployment is the central obstacle to practical WiFi sensing: a pipeline reaching 0.89+ top-1 in its training environments collapses to 0.408 under Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation with only K-shot labels. A ceiling analysis shows the collapse is not an alignment problem: the action signal is strong across seen environments (about 0.89 K10), environment identity is decodable from the encoder (0.965), and the failure concentrates in the encoder's extrapolation to the novel environment. A pre-registered falsification chain confirms that "align the domains" methods–training-time alignment, readout-level prototype alignment, adversarial confusion, and covariance/subspace alignment (CORAL -3.8pp, subspace -8.3pp)–degrade performance, and that source-domain statistics anti-correlate with cross-environment contribution. The effective levers lie elsewhere; we combine them into Dec-H: (i) closed-form source within-class whitening, provably re-geometrizing the readout's L2 regularization (+8.6pp, zero cost); (ii) profile-mixing augmentation (+1.0pp); (iii) few-shot adaptation with alternating whitening refit (+1.5pp; fixed preconditioners are 20/20 negative); (iv) heterogeneous decision ensembles (+1.7pp); homogeneous scaling and source-weighted stacking are saturated or harmful. Dec-H reaches 0.560 K10 (0.812 K40), +15.2pp over the baseline, consistent across all four environments and seeds; all thirteen configurations were pre-registered with frozen criteria.
entries.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Preprint of a manuscript submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

entries.title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
entries.abstract: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for presentation at IEEE CloudNet 2026

entries.title: Signed Powers-of-Two Greedy Vector Approximation of Zadoff-Chu Sequences
entries.abstract: This paper explores the use of sums of signed powers-of-two (SOPOT) for a representation suitable for multiplierless applications of ZC sequences, where multiplications are reduced to a prescribed number of shift-and-add operations. The SOPOT representation is achieved using a greedy algorithm that outperforms other approaches for multiplierless approximations, such as CORDIC and CSD. The proposed algorithm is based on the matching pursuits using generalized bit planes (MPGBP), and the proposed modification enables robustness to hyperparameter tuning. The resulting sequences retain, to some extent, the good autocorrelation properties of ZC, as shown in a matched-filter detection simulation. This corroborates to their use in various practical applications across mainstream cellular systems and devices requiring moderate computational cost.

entries.title: Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
entries.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to an IEEE conference

entries.title: A closed-loop agentic research environment for MRI development within Siemens IDEA platform
entries.abstract: Motivation: Testing new ideas in MRI can require substantial effort to learn sequence programming and reconstruction tools and to debug implementations before the scientific question can be addressed. Goals: Reduce the implementation and debugging burden of testing MRI ideas while retaining researcher control of scientific decisions. Approach: We developed an environment where LLM agents develop sequences in the native Siemens IDEA platform, evaluate them through Bloch simulation and reconstruction, and further iteratively refine them using scanner feedback. Results: As test cases, the agentic environment was used to implement and validate a GIRF-based gradient-calibration sequence and reconstruction in approximately 4 hours, and to develop and optimize a rapid 3-second multichannel calibration scan in approximately 12 hours of researcher-guided iteration.

entries.title: Lightweight Low-Frequency Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring via Karhunen-Loève Feature Distillation and Temporal Convolutional Networks
entries.abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical enabler for demand-side management which allows for smart grid optimization. A deployment-ready NILM solution necessitates three key features: accurate disaggregation, low-frequency sampling, and low computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight, edge-oriented NILM framework that combines activity-boundary-aware synthetic data augmentation with Karhunen-Loève Transform (KLT) feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The augmentation stage extracts and recombines complete or near-complete appliance activation segments so that the model can be trained without new fully labeled household aggregates. The KLT filter bank extracts decorrelated, appliance-informed temporal features which are then fed into a compact TCN along with the original aggregate for energy disaggregation. Evaluations on two standard NILM datasets, UK-DALE and REDD, at 10-s sampling and with leave-one-house-out testing, demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior disaggregation accuracy relative to NILMFormer, BERT4NILM, BiLSTM, and BiGRU. The computational footprint of the framework is 31,009 parameters, the fewest of the five models compared, and on a single CPU thread it needs 2.78 ms per 1000 samples, 84-95% less than the baselines. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for low-frequency smart-meter NILM.
entries.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid. S. Peeris, P. Thennakoon and P. Sumanasekara contributed equally

entries.title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
entries.abstract: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.

entries.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for CKM-Assisted Network Deployment Optimization
entries.abstract: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) offer reusable, site-specific radio priors to facilitate environment-aware network planning. However, deploying heterogeneous network nodes to meet diverse performance requirements in complex environments is challenging and requires executable workflows that coordinate scene preparation, candidate-site specification, CKM construction, optimization, and validation. This paper presents a large language model (LLM)-orchestrated agent framework for CKM-assisted network deployment optimization, where an LLM translates high-level requirements into modular, typed, and reproducible planning workflows. In this framework, an LLM layer interprets intent, selects modules, and populates normalized configurations; physics-grounded modules generate scene, CKM, optimization, and validation artifacts; and a deterministic guarded controller performs validation-guided refinement. A common target-candidate-CKM-optimizer interface supports the registration and composition of compatible planning modules, with CKM backends, samplers, and solvers remaining replaceable. We instantiate the proposed framework for base station (BS) deployment, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. An urban-block case study demonstrates automatic scene consistency checks, bounded BS/IRS deployment refinement, and collision- and radio-feasible UAV planning.

entries.title: 20 ghz longitudinal surface acoustic wave resonators in 100-nm x-cut lithium niobate on silicon carbide
entries.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15 GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling (k²). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high k² in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7 GHz and reaching a k² of 8.1%, a maximum Bode Q of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24 GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength (λ) keeps the normalized LN thickness (h_()LN/λ) large, sustaining both k² and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing λ from 292 to 471 nm lowers h_()LN/λ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05 km/s, within 1.1% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and k² falls from its 8.1% peak at λ= 322 nm to 1.7% at λ= 471 nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for λ≥518 nm (h_()LN/λ≤0.19), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5% of its maximum for h_()LN/λ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

entries.title: WiFo-D: Wireless Foundation Model Based on Discrete Representations
entries.abstract: Wireless foundation models have shown strong generalization capabilities across heterogeneous wireless tasks and configurations. However, most existing models rely on continuous representations, limiting ultra-low-overhead channel state information (CSI) feedback, few-shot generalization, and robustness to noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a wireless foundation model based on discrete representations (WiFo-D), which learns multi-granularity discrete CSI representations. It comprises a CSI encoder, multi-codebook vector quantization, and a modulation-based decoder, with the learned token maps and quantized features supporting multi-rate CSI feedback, CSI reconstruction, and diverse CSI-related downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong CSI feedback performance at an ultra-low latent compression ratio of 1/32 with 3 bits per token, reducing normalized mean square error (NMSE) by more than 4.7 dB compared with the strongest baseline. Furthermore, for frequency-domain prediction with limited training samples, WiFo-D improves generalization and noise robustness over continuous-representation-based methods. The results also demonstrate its superiority across downstream tasks, including beam prediction, wireless localization, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight identification.

entries.title: Distributed Fiber Monitoring on a Coherent DSP ASIC: Implementation of Longitudinal Power Monitoring
entries.abstract: Coherent DSP ASICs and transceivers to date report a rich set of optical link metrics, yet these remain cumulative over the link and provide no spatial localization. This paper presents the implementation design of fiber-longitudinal power monitoring (LPM), which recovers spatially resolved power profiles from received traffic, on a coherent DSP ASIC chip. We first identify the challenges specific to DSP implementation, and describe the enabling algorithm and architecture. We then present the key design considerations for retaining the estimation fidelity of the on-chip LPM during in-service operation. On this basis, we implement LPM on a coherent DSP, a 3-nm 800G low-power DSP ASIC housed in an OSFP pluggable module, which constitutes, to our knowledge, the first coherent DSP ASIC and transceiver to perform distributed fiber monitoring and data communication simultaneously. The on-chip LPM is experimentally validated over links of up to 1005 km using 400ZR+ and 800ZR+ traffic, with no measurable impact on Q factor or module power consumption. Multi-vendor interoperability is also demonstrated, where the on-chip LPM operates on signals transmitted by third-party transceivers. These results extend coherent DSPs from cumulative to spatially resolved monitoring, allowing pluggable transceivers, deployable from DCI to long-haul, to act not only as cost-efficient transmission elements but also as distributed monitoring points across diverse optical network infrastructure.

entries.title: Conditional-Hierarchical Open-Set Deep Learning for Robust Radio Signals Intelligence
entries.abstract: This paper proposes an open-set radio-frequency (RF) deep learning (DL) framework that jointly performs conditionally hierarchical multi-level radio signal classification and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. To exploit image-based classification models, the raw radio samples are transformed into time-frequency representations using the short time Fourier transform (STFT) to pre-process the radio signals. A lightweight novel architecture using neural network (CNN), that applies con- ditional hierarchical multi-task classification heads, is introduced, and compared to two baselines including: (1) The conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) and (2) Swin-T model with multitask classification heads, where the model accuracy and complexity perspectives are considered for the comparison. Moreover, to address open-set scenarios, we introduce the fusion of two OOD detectors each of which is fitted to a Gaussian mixture model by using the learned feature space (e.g. the feature embeddings and logits) from the multi-head classifica- tion network. The overall training process is achieved on two stages following a post-hoc design: the in-set classification neural network is trained first, then the learnable parameters are frozen in the evaluation mode to process the training dataset again to aggregate the embeddings and logits used to fit the GMMs for OOD detection. Moreover, a proof of concept using experimental setup is implemented to validate the operation of the introduced models and algorithms in practical scenarios. The simulation- based trained model is fine-tuned using experimentally measured radio signals. For the experimental setup, a USRP-B210 acting as a transmitter, and an edge Deepwave Air-T software-defined radio, which is equipped with the fine-tuned neural networks is used as a detector or receiver.

entries.title: AE-DISC: Automorphism Ensemble Direct-Invocation Successive Cancellation for Low-Latency Decoding
entries.abstract: Emerging applications in hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) demand channel decoders that deliver deterministic performance under stringent latency and reliability constraints. While Polar codes are well suited for this scenario due to their strong error-correction capability, conventional successive cancellation (SC) decoding exhibits inherent serial dependencies that lead to high decoding latency. This paper presents the automorphism ensemble direct-invocation successive cancellation (AE-DISC) decoder, a low-latency framework that enables the concurrent computation of the left and right decoding subtrees in the SC process, yielding substantial speed-ups. By exploiting permutation automorphisms, AE-DISC decoding further improves error-correction performance. Simulation results demonstrate that AE-DISC attains up to 1.4 dB gain over the 5G SC baseline and surpasses layered min-sum (LMS) low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders at a frame error rate (FER) of 10⁻⁶, while maintaining fixed algorithmic complexity. Both theoretical analysis and application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) synthesis results further show up to 2 times decoding speed-up relative to fast simplified successive cancellation (FSSC).

entries.title: Adaptive Filtering With Reduced Computational Complexity Using SOPOT Arithmetic
entries.abstract: Implementing finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive filters by employing the sums of signed-powers-of-two (SOPOT) arithmetic may lead to simpler hardware and consequently reduced power consumption. In this paper, one evaluates the effects of SOPOT arithmetic on the adaptive filter's recursion algorithms. The filters' coefficients and algorithms' underlying variables are fully operated using SOPOT arithmetic in the whole iterative process. More specifically, one evaluates convergence rate, numerical stability, and accuracy since using few signed-powers-of-two (SPT) terms propagates numerical errors during the adaptive cycle that may impair the algorithm behavior. The SOPOT approximations are obtained through the technique known as Matching Pursuits with Generalized Bit-Plane (MPGBP) algorithm, with notable cost-performance trade-off and low computational complexity. Results are provided for the Least-Mean-Squares (LMS), the Normalized Least-Mean-Squares (NLMS) and the Recursive-Least-Squares (RLS) algorithms, considering adaptive filters employed for system identification and change detection.
entries.journalRef: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers (Volume: 69, Issue: 2, February 2022)

entries.title: Greedy Vector Approximation Based on Rotation for Multiplierless Complex Products
entries.abstract: This paper proposes a greedy approximation algorithm for performing complex-valued inner products in multiplierless hardware. The matching pursuits for accurate rotation approximation (MPARA) algorithm approximates the tangent of the phase of complex elements as a sum of signed powers of two (SOPOT) representation, enabling multiplierless hardware for complex-valued multiplication. The proposed algorithm outperforms other state-of-the-art approximation methods for approximating the twiddle factors of a fast Fourier transform (FFT).

entries.title: Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping
entries.abstract: The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover fractional abundances. The severe lack of standard indices necessitates the use of complex, data-driven unmixing models. Complex unmixing models require dense, well-distributed manifolds, whereas ground-truth datasets are sparse and expensive. To better leverage the information content in existing ground-truth datasets, this study presents a framework that decouples interpolation and abundance-mapping estimation via an intermediary conditional data generator, contrasting with traditional single-model unmixing pipelines. This decoupling enables the inclusion of physical prior knowledge about spectra, which is not natively accessible to unmixing models, thereby artificially expanding the dataset to serve as a Monte Carlo approximation of the population risk. To test this hypothesis, we have proposed two generator models: a 1D Conditional U-Net with Conformer Layers (GD-Streamline) and a Dual-Path Transformer Conditional Variational AutoEncoder (TCVAE), and two unmixing models: Multi-Layered Perceptrons (MLP) and Fourier Neural Operators (FNO). The results of the study indicate a need for rigorous integration and introduction of spectral priors within the scope of the proposed decoupling framework to prevent domain and mode collapse and hallucination by the generator models; otherwise, this leads to falsely approximated data manifolds, ultimately resulting in unsatisfactory and out-of-distribution unmixing performance.

entries.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
entries.abstract: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.

entries.title: Spectrally Correlated Frequency Spreading Codes for FRESH Filtering-based Interference Cancellation
entries.abstract: Frequency shift (FRESH) filters can achieve co-channel interference cancellation by exploiting spectral correlation statistics of both the desired and interfering signals. In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, spectral correlation can be introduced in a structured way by symbol repetition across subcarriers. While this repetition generally requires duplicating symbols by an integer multiple of 2+ times (significantly impacting spectral efficiency), in this work it is shown that applying an incomplete spreading code, that trades spectral efficiency, to the desired signal can control its spectral correlation properties at redundancy factors less than 2. The distribution of the spectral correlation across frequencies determines the level of protection against interference at a given frequency. We introduce the design of frequency spreading codes that provide uniform spectral correlation distribution across frequencies, which provides equal interference cancellation capability independent of the center frequency of the interfering signal. The introduced spreading code can achieve arbitrary code rates while possessing two important properties: 1) semi-orthogonality and 2) spectral correlation uniformity. We evaluate the BER performance at very low signal-to-interference levels SIR$=0, 5 $ dB comparing spreading, LDPC, and LDPC+spreading at equal code rates.

entries.title: Slim-Mamba: An Efficient and Reconfigurable Mamba-Based Accelerator for Massive MIMO Indoor Localization
entries.abstract: Using real-world massive MIMO measurements from the LuViRA dataset, we present a system-level solution combining Mamba-based model development and hardware acceleration for indoor localization. Three Mamba-based models are explored: the original Mamba architecture, CMamba, a channel-correlation-enhanced state-space model designed to exploit correlations across input channels, and our proposed Slim-Mamba. Hardware implementation and bottleneck analysis are then used to guide further model simplification and optimization. The resulting Slim-Mamba simplifies the original Mamba selective state-space block into a lightweight gated recurrent update, preserving temporal state modelling and output gating while reducing the complexity of the selective-scan computation. The deployed model contains 816k trainable parameters and has a model size of 3.40MB under FP32 precision while maintaining high localization accuracy. The corresponding accelerator provides a reconfigurable architecture with a highly parallel MAC array optimized for matrix-vector operations and fine-grained pipelining, improving resource utilization and reducing inference latency. The hardware-aware fixed-point model achieves a mean localization error of 0.14m, closely matching the floating-point baseline. Implemented on a Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU102 FPGA, the four-block backbone has an estimated serial latency of 212.04us per token at 100MHz.

entries.title: Risk-Aware Safe Hierarchical Learning for Robust eMBB-URLLC Resource Allocation in O-RAN
entries.abstract: Joint resource allocation for enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) must satisfy stringent URLLC latency and reliability requirements while maintaining eMBB throughput under uncertain traffic and channel conditions. Existing learning-based allocators often optimize average aggregate performance without explicitly accounting for prediction errors, potentially resulting in severe service degradation for individual users. We propose a risk-aware safe hierarchical learning framework for Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) that learns resource-feasible allocations using service-cost penalties and a per-user URLLC service test. A non-real-time policy determines slice-level resource-block and power budgets, near-real-time policies allocate resource blocks and transmit power among users, and an execution-time safety layer checks per-user URLLC service and corrects allocations through bounded resource transfers when feasible. A deterministic per-user service test, derived using protected rates accounting for channel state information prediction errors and conformal upper bounds on traffic demand, ensures satisfaction of the probabilistic URLLC requirement. Service-specific conditional value-at-risk objectives prioritize users with the highest URLLC deadline-miss ratios and lowest eMBB rates. Experimental results show that, under nominal load, the proposed framework is the only evaluated method that satisfies both the URLLC deadline-miss target and worst-user eMBB rate criterion on average. It reduces the mean miss ratio by 64% relative to the best baseline in this metric and achieves the highest worst-user eMBB rate.
entries.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Communications

entries.title: Constellation Shaping for OFDM-ISAC Systems: A Systematic and Experimental Comparison
entries.abstract: Emerging integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems reuse the communications signal for radar-like sensing to provide environmental awareness. However, this integrated design imposes conflicting constraints on the modulation format, as communications systems use higher-order modulation formats while sensing systems use unit-modulus signals, making constellation shaping a key performance driver in ISAC systems. This paper develops a unified analytical and experimental framework for constellation shaping in monostatic orthogonal frequency division multiplexing ISAC systems and systematically analyzes its interaction with the three canonical sensing channel estimators (SCEs): the matched filter, the reciprocal filter, and the Wiener filter (WF). We begin by deriving constellation-dependent image signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (ISINR) expressions for the SCEs that account for practical effects such as windowing and multi target scenarios. Based on this, we derive the corresponding entropy-maximizing channel input distributions. We generalize an autoencoder framework to optimize geometric, probabilistic, including conventional and generalized low-complexity probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS), and joint constellation shaping across all three SCEs. Extensive simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments validate the derived ISINR and show that sensing performance is governed by the SCE choice, while communications performance is dominated by the shaping method. Notably, the WF combined with joint shaping achieves the best ISAC trade-off. Low-complexity PAS variants closely approach this performance, offering a flexible trade-off and outperforming legacy modulation formats.

entries.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
entries.abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

entries.title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
entries.abstract: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

entries.title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
entries.abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

entries.title: Towards Deep Learning-Based Linear Assignment Problem Solvers for Multi-Object Tracking
entries.abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates deep learning (DL)-based linear assignment problem (LAP) solvers as a replacement for the classical Hungarian algorithm in multi-object tracking (MOT) systems. Three representative neural models are studied, namely a convolutional network (CNN), a graph neural network (GNN), and the graph-based linear assignment network (GLAN). A cost-matrix embedding is introduced so that a single model operates on cost matrices of any size, as required in MOT where the number of objects varies over time, without training a separate model for each input shape. Extensive simulations show that the embedding improves the accuracy of the neural solvers (i.e., CNN and GNN), while GLAN attains the best accuracy among them. These solvers are then integrated into a generalized labeled multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) tracker and evaluated on the WILDTRACK dataset, where GLAN yields tracking accuracy close to the Hungarian reference and comparable to recent DL-based trackers.

entries.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
entries.abstract: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly classified. To address this, we propose the novel PACT (Piecewise Adaptation via Chart Transport). PACT partitions the frozen source embedding space into local charts and learns lightweight residual transports for the regions affected by each new condition. An explicit identity path is always retained, and a learned gate softly selects among the identity and accumulated transports for each input. The pretrained TSFM encoder, classifier head, and previously learned transports remain fixed. With only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no condition identity at test time, PACT maintains an average macro-F1 above 0.95 across a four-condition bearing-fault stream. Under homogeneous tasks and label spaces, similar retention-adaptation behavior is observed across public benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Sachithx/PACT.

entries.title: Toward Massive MIMO HAPS Networks: Antenna Architectures and Design
entries.abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPS) are expected to become an important component of sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks by providing wide-area wireless connectivity through massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) technology. As the communication performance of HAPS systems is fundamentally determined by the antenna array architecture, efficient antenna design has become a critical research topic. Motivated by these considerations, this article provides a comprehensive overview of antenna array design for mMIMO-enabled HAPS systems and proposes two novel antenna architectures to improve antenna-user alignment and communication performance. Specifically, the representative applications of mMIMO-enabled HAPS are first introduced, followed by the key design requirements for HAPS antenna arrays. Representative antenna architectures are then systematically reviewed and compared under a unified simulation framework based on the 3GPP NTN channel model. Finally, several promising research directions are discussed to provide insights into the design of next-generation intelligent HAPS antenna systems.

entries.title: EEGSync: Unitary Temporal Alignment Method for Naturalistic and Resting-State EEG
entries.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) studies increasingly use naturalistic and resting-state paradigms that lack discrete event timing. These recordings contain structured oscillatory activity but often lack repeated stimulus onsets to define a shared time clock across trials or participants. We introduce EEGSync, a complex-valued unitary Procrustes temporal alignment method for band-limited analytic EEG signals. EEGSync represents each subject as a matrix of complex oscillatory trajectories and solves a unitary Procrustes problem, mapping a target subject into the temporal coordinate system of a reference or group template. The method is computationally tractable through an economy-SVD factorization that avoids constructing the full temporal operator. This alignment strictly preserves original pairwise relationships and power across EEG channels. The unitary transformation aligns latent temporal structure rather than estimating a physical clock offset. Consequently, nonlinear instantaneous measures like phase-locking value, amplitude-envelope correlation, and phase-amplitude coupling are not guaranteed to be invariant. This framing makes EEGSync highly suitable for naturalistic shared-stimulus data, and potentially useful for resting-state data as a covariance-preserving latent manifold alignment. Evaluated via subject-independent cross-validation across physiological and clinical settings, EEGSync-based features achieved an AUROC of 0.9600 and 89.45% maximum classification accuracy in eyes-open versus eyes-closed state discrimination. For Alzheimer's disease versus healthy control classification, the highest AUROC reached 0.9272 in eyes-closed recordings, with further discrimination under eyes-open photostimulation. These findings suggest temporal alignment captures discriminative information complementing conventional spectral and statistical EEG features.

entries.title: Convolution-Augmented Transformer for Robust Blind CFO Estimation in LEO Satellite Communication System
entries.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communications are essential for achieving ubiquitous global connectivity. However, the high mobility of LEO satellites induces massive Doppler shifts and fast time-varying fading, severely impairing signal synchronization. Accurate Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) estimation is critical for receiver synchronization. Nevertheless, conventional estimators and deep learning approaches often degrade significantly under highly dynamic, low-SNR conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Convolution Augmented Transformer architecture for robust, blind CFO estimation in LEO communication systems. Initially, to overcome the inherent limitations of standard linear embedding layers in capturing nonlinear phase rotations, we construct a multi-domain input feature that encompasses in-phase/quadrature (I/Q), polar, and statistical autocorrelation properties. Subsequently, a Convolutional Pre-Denoising (CPD) module, integrating multi-scale dilated convolutions and an attention mechanism, is deployed at the front end to adaptively suppress localized noise and extract robust spatiotemporal representations. These refined latent features are then processed by a Transformer encoder to explicitly track global, long-range phase dependencies. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed data-driven approach significantly outperforms conventional estimation algorithms, achieving enhanced estimation accuracy and superior resilience in highly dynamic LEO environments.

entries.title: Multidimensional Source-Space MEG Representation of Network Imbalance in ADHD
entries.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with an atypical imbalance between the default mode network (DMN) and task-control systems. However, compressing neural activity into a single macroscopic imbalance measure may obscure individual neurophysiological differences. To address this, we leveraged the source-orientation selectivity and related measurement properties of resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) to establish a multidimensional source-space network representation in 21 individuals with ADHD and 21 healthy controls. We defined the macroscopic imbalance in relative Alpha activity between the DMN and task-control systems as the Core, and expanded its constituent information along three dimensions: spatial sources, spectral composition, and temporal network organization: into in-depth measures, assessed for stability, robustness, and complementarity. We found that the ADHD group exhibited a significant Core Alpha imbalance, driven mainly by task-control regions, while the multidimensional expansion revealed complementary ADHD-related neurophysiological information not fully represented by the Core, suggesting that similar macroscopic imbalances may reflect distinct underlying physiological states. Across 40 exploratory within-cohort held-out evaluations with separate development and test subsets, mean ROC-AUC increased from 0.7607 (Core-only) to 0.8995 with multidimensional inputs and to 0.9051 with the final ensemble, and mean accuracy increased from 71.43% to 79.82%. These findings suggest that multidimensional source-space expansion can further clarify the neurophysiological composition of ADHD-related network imbalance and improve individual-level discrimination, offering an interpretable framework potentially applicable to other brain disorders characterized by network imbalance.
entries.comment: Submitted to IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics (JBHI)

entries.title: Physical Layer Security for Digital Semantic Communication: A Bit-Level Perspective
entries.abstract: Digital semantic communication requires reliable recovery of task-relevant information at a legitimate receiver while limiting source reconstruction by an eavesdropper. Uniform bit protection, however, does not account for the heterogeneous reliability and secrecy requirements of semantic bits. This paper proposes a bit-level physical layer security (PLS) framework that learns these requirements and incorporates them into physical-layer resource allocation. We first introduce a wiretap semantic feature channel whose two-stage training learns per-bit target bit-flip probabilities for the legitimate receiver (Bob) and the eavesdropper (Eve). These targets characterize the reliability requirements at Bob and the secrecy protection requirements against Eve. Based on the learned targets, we formulate a joint power and artificial-noise (AN) allocation problem for a multiple-input single-output wiretap channel under a worst-case angular-separation model. For a given target profile, the optimal information-AN power split admits a closed-form solution, and the per-bit power allocation is obtained by water-filling. We further develop a leakage-aware selection method among multiple learned-target profiles and extend the design to multiple-input multiple-output channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a better trade-off between preserving reconstruction quality at Bob and degrading that at Eve than uniform power allocation and the evaluated learning-based secure semantic communication schemes.

entries.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
entries.abstract: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.
entries.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures; submitted to IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems (TAES)

entries.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
entries.abstract: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of 3^(3/4) per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion. We give an explicit expression for the number of settings needed to reach a target fraction, accurate up to a remainder that reduces to a small oscillation for many qubits, and show that random sampling is asymptotically optimal up to a factor of less than 1.69. Coverage does not determine what a setting contributes to an estimator. Observables covered by one setting are estimated from the same outcomes, so their estimates are correlated. We quantify this correlation through the design effect of a setting, which equals the squared Pauli expectation that the setting captures and depends on the target state. We derive its mean over settings in closed form for every state and show that it can be estimated without bias from the measurement data. In simulations on six qubits, measuring settings needs 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring the same number of observables independently. At high coverage, fitting the outcome histograms instead of averaged estimates roughly halves the reconstruction error, mainly because the fit counts how many settings cover each observable. The correlation itself costs such a fit about a factor of two, and a larger design effect signals more to gain from modeling it.

entries.title: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation
entries.abstract: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, and 1 table. An 18-page supplement is included as an ancillary file

entries.title: Towards Environment-Aware 6G Network Planning: An Any-to-Any Channel Knowledge Map Approach
entries.abstract: Planning sixth-generation (6G) networks for reliable coverage across diverse environments is challenging, as it requires channel knowledge between candidate network node locations and potential service regions. This article proposes an environment-aware network planning framework based on any-to-any (X2X) channel knowledge maps (CKMs), which characterize channels between arbitrary transmitter-receiver location pairs. Within this framework, we first construct X2X CKMs from environmental information, sparse channel measurements, or both, with map types and spatial resolutions selected according to the planning task. We then use these maps to predict coverage and optimize network deployment and configuration subject to service requirements and practical constraints, while accounting for subsequent network operation. Finally, field measurements assess channel prediction accuracy and deployment performance, providing feedback for CKM correction and deployment refinement. We discuss implementation methods and tradeoffs across these stages. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the framework for indoor intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment and outdoor base station (BS) deployment. Live-network trials further demonstrate coverage gains from IRS deployment and BS reconfiguration, with measurement feedback supporting CKM calibration and configuration refinement.

entries.title: Fisher Information Characterization in GNSS DPE under Multipath-Induced Channel Uncertainty
entries.abstract: The availability and utilization of Fisher information in global navigation satellite system (GNSS) direct position estimation (DPE) under multipath-induced channel uncertainty are investigated. First, a unified estimation-theoretic framework is developed to characterize information mapping and utilization across direct and two-step receivers. Next, a scalar-equivalent statistical channel model for short-delay multipath is established via least-squares (LS) projection. Based on this model, receiver-state Cramér-Rao bounds (CRBs) are derived under perfect and statistical channel knowledge, while misspecified CRBs (MCRBs) are derived under a simplified deterministic complex-gain model that neglects channel uncertainty. The closed-form approximations and asymptotic analyses of the derived bounds further reveal how channel uncertainty affects different components of waveform-domain Fisher information. Our results reveal that: 1) DPE and fully coupled two-step estimation achieve comparable accuracy, whereas the performance loss caused by sequential decoupling substantially exceeds the additional loss from suboptimal weighting; 2) under statistical channel knowledge, improving received signal quality does not necessarily yield noticeable positioning gains; 3) positioning information remains available even as the coherent channel mean vanishes; and 4) neglecting channel randomness causes the MCRBs to diverge in this limit and can introduce positioning error floors that become more pronounced with longer observations.
